newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon economic growth slows in January.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon economic growth slows in January.

text.p: Lebanon's economic activity fell in January to its lowest level in eight months, the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest economic bulletin on Wednesday.
The central bank said its coincident indicator of economic activity stood at 166.0 in January against 168.3 at the end of December. This compared with 155.9 in January 1996.
It was the lowest level since May 1996 when the indicator stood at 164.7.

Construction activity, one of the important indicators of economic activity in post-war Lebanon, continued a downward trend as cement deliveries fell 18.6 percent on the month to 239,000 tonnes. It was 11.6 percent up on a year-on-year basis.
The January balance of trade produced a deficit of $426 million -- down from January 1996 deficit of $493 million.
Imports declined 9.8 percent to $514.7 million while exports grew 13.9 percent to $88.5 million, the bank said.
Foreign debt rose slightly to $1.797 billion from $1.791 billion at the end of December, it added.
Net total public debt rose to 16,433 billion pounds in January from 16,138 billion at the end of 1996. It stood at 11,690 in January 1996, the bank said.
"The increase in debt was mainly due to the rise in net domestic debt which reached 13,647.2 billion at end of January 1997, against 13,358.2 billion at end December 1996," it added.
The balance of payments registered a surplus of $203.6 million against a deficit of $64.1 million in January 1996.
"Monetary stability was reflected through low inflation and an appreciation of the Lebanese pound," the bank said without giving the rate of inflation or other indicators of inflationary levels.
Last month, the Lebanese Banks Association said the Consumer Price Index rose 2.9 percent in January.
